items.title: Crew-neck T-shirts
items.why: A crew neck in a structured cotton keeps attention up near the shoulders.
items.tip: The shoulder seam should sit on your shoulder bone and the hem just past your belt.

items.title: Casual shirts
items.why: Chest pockets and a firm collar add interest above the waist.
items.tip: Untucked shirts should end around mid-fly; longer hems are meant to be tucked.

items.title: Casual button-downs (camp collar)
items.why: A print on top draws the eye upward.
items.tip: Small, tonal prints are easier to wear than large busy ones.

items.title: Straight-fit jeans
items.why: A straight leg falls smoothly from the hip without clinging.
items.tip: Aim for a slight break, or none, where the hem meets your shoe.

items.title: Chinos
items.why: A mid-to-dark straight chino keeps the lower half simple.
items.tip: A mid-rise works for most; a small cuff suits loafers and sneakers.

items.title: Slim or tapered jeans
items.why: Slim through the thigh with a gentle taper to the ankle.
items.tip: Leave room to sit comfortably — a little stretch helps.

items.title: Bomber jackets
items.why: Volume at the chest and shoulders balances the hips.
items.tip: The hem should land at your belt line.

items.title: Denim jackets
items.why: A structured shoulder broadens the top line.
items.tip: Wear it over a tee or hoodie; size up only if you layer knits.

items.title: Blazers
items.why: Structured shoulders balance wider hips.
items.tip: Shoulder seams end at your shoulder; let a little shirt cuff show.

items.title: Kurtas
items.why: A kurta ending mid-thigh or at the knee falls smoothly past the hips.
items.tip: Hip-to-knee length works for most heights; shorter kurtas pair well with jeans.

items.title: Sherwanis
items.why: Structured shoulders balance the lower body.
items.tip: Get the shoulders fitted; the length usually sits just below the knee.

items.title: Kurta-pyjama sets
items.why: A kurta with churidar or straight pyjama, matching or in contrast.
items.tip: A tapered churidar suits shorter kurtas; straight pyjamas suit longer ones.

items.title: Clean sneakers
items.why: Minimal leather or canvas sneakers.
items.tip: White or off-white goes with almost everything — keep them clean.

items.title: Loafers
items.why: Slip-ons that dress up chinos and tailored trousers.
items.tip: No-show socks keep the ankle clean in warm weather.

items.title: Derby shoes
items.why: Open-laced leather shoes that suit wider feet.
items.tip: Match your belt to your shoes.

items.title: Belts
items.why: A leather belt matched to your shoes.
items.tip: A 3–3.5 cm width suits most trousers.

items.title: Watches
items.why: A simple dial on a leather or metal strap.
items.tip: Match the strap to your belt and shoes, or the metal to your undertone.

items.title: Ties & pocket squares
items.why: A tie in an accent shade with a pocket square that picks up a second colour.
items.tip: Don't match the tie and pocket square exactly — echo a colour instead.

shape_notes: Structure and detail on top — collars, chest pockets, structured shoulders — balance the hips.
Darker, straight or relaxed trousers keep the lower half simple.
Avoid very skinny trousers that emphasise the hip-to-ankle contrast.

fit_guide.tip: Shoulder seams should sit at the edge of your shoulders; most fit problems elsewhere can be tailored.
A slight break (one soft fold at the shoe) suits most trousers; slim trousers look best with no break.
Untucked shirts should end around mid-fly; if it covers your seat, it's meant to be tucked.
A blazer should cover your seat; casual jackets look best ending at the belt.
Go from thin to thick: tee, then shirt or overshirt, then jacket.
Linen and cotton for hot, humid days; wool blends for air-conditioned offices and cooler months.

items.title: Off-shoulder tops
items.why: Width at the shoulders balances the hips.
items.tip: A wide elastic band stays put more comfortably.

items.title: Boat-neck tops
items.why: A wide neckline balances the hips.
items.tip: Tuck the front in to show the waist.

items.title: Puff-sleeve tops
items.why: Volume at the shoulders balances the hips.
items.tip: Keep bottoms simple to balance the sleeves.

items.title: Wide-leg trousers
items.why: A wide leg falls straight from the hip.
items.tip: Hem them to just skim the floor in the shoes you'll wear.

items.title: Flared trousers
items.why: The flare balances the line from hip to hem.
items.tip: Wear with a small heel or platform to keep the line long.

items.title: Bootcut jeans
items.why: Falls smoothly from the hip.
items.tip: Mid or dark washes look polished.

items.title: Fit-and-flare dresses
items.why: Fitted at the waist, flowing over the hips.
items.tip: A knee-length hem is the easiest to wear day to night.

items.title: Shift dresses
items.why: An easy, straight shape.
items.tip: Add a belt only if you want to mark the waist.

items.title: Bodycon dresses
items.why: A close fit that follows your silhouette.
items.tip: Thicker, structured knits are more forgiving than thin jersey.

items.title: Cropped jackets
items.why: Ends above the hips and highlights the waist.
items.tip: Pair with high-waisted bottoms.

items.title: Belted blazers
items.why: Structure that keeps the waist visible.
items.tip: Belt at the natural waist, not the hips.

items.title: Soft-shoulder blazers
items.why: Soft-structured blazers without heavy shoulder pads.
items.tip: Wear open for a long vertical line.

items.title: Sarees & blouses
items.why: A fitted blouse with interest at the neckline draws the eye up.
items.tip: Lighter fabrics like georgette or chiffon drape closely; silks and organza hold shape.

items.title: Kurtas & kurta sets
items.why: An A-line kurta flows past the hips.
items.tip: Side slits make long kurtas easier to move in.

items.title: Lehengas
items.why: A flared skirt, blouse and dupatta for weddings and festive events.
items.tip: Lighter lehengas are easier to dance in.

items.title: Block heels
items.why: Stable, comfortable height.
items.tip: 5–7 cm is comfortable for long days.

items.title: Flats, juttis & loafers
items.why: Comfortable everyday shoes.
items.tip: Juttis suit kurta sets; loafers suit trousers.

items.title: Sneakers
items.why: Clean sneakers for casual outfits and travel.
items.tip: White sneakers go with dresses as well as jeans.

items.title: Handbags
items.why: A structured tote for work and a small bag for evenings.
items.tip: A neutral from your palette goes with most outfits.

items.title: Corset & wide belts
items.why: Add waist definition and a modern finishing touch.
items.tip: Wear over dresses or long shirts.

items.title: Scarves & dupattas
items.why: A quick way to wear your best colours near your face.
items.tip: Drape vertically for length, or loop for warmth.

shape_notes: Boat, off-shoulder and square necklines bring attention upward.
Darker or simpler bottoms with brighter tops create balance.
Straight-leg, bootcut and flared shapes fall smoothly from the hip.

fit_guide.tip: Choose one focus area per outfit — a fitted top with relaxed bottoms, or the reverse.
Hem trousers for the shoes you'll wear most; midi skirts look best ending just below the widest part of the calf.
A front tuck, a belt or a wrap is optional — use it when you want to mark the waist.
Long open layers add length; cropped layers mark the waist.
Cotton, linen and rayon breathe in heat; structured fabrics hold shape for work.
If you can't sit, reach or walk easily, the fit is wrong — not you.

items.title: Oversized T-shirts
items.why: A roomier top balances the hips.
items.tip: Balance the volume with straight or tapered bottoms.

items.title: Hoodies & sweatshirts
items.why: Upper-body volume balances the hips.
items.tip: Choose a hem with a rib so it sits neatly at the hip.

items.title: Relaxed shirts
items.why: A loose cotton or linen shirt, worn open or buttoned.
items.tip: Roll the sleeves twice for an easy look.

items.title: Straight-leg denim
items.why: A straight, mid-rise jean.
items.tip: A slight crop shows off sneakers.

items.title: Relaxed trousers
items.why: Pleated or elastic-waist trousers with drape.
items.tip: Taper slightly at the ankle if you're shorter.

items.title: Cargo & utility trousers
items.why: Practical trousers with pockets.
items.tip: Keep the top streamlined.

items.title: Denim jackets
items.why: Structure at the shoulders balances the hips.
items.tip: Size up for a boxy fit over hoodies.

items.title: Chore jackets & overshirts
items.why: Boxy cotton jackets with patch pockets.
items.tip: Wear open over a tee or knit.

items.title: Minimalist layering pieces
items.why: Light cardigans, vests and zip knits.
items.tip: Stick to two or three palette shades for easy mixing.

items.title: Straight kurtas with trousers
items.why: A simple straight kurta worn with straight trousers or jeans.
items.tip: Plain fabrics with a contrast placket keep it versatile.

items.title: Bandhgala & short jackets
items.why: A structured band-collar jacket over a kurta or tee.
items.tip: Dark palette shades look festive without being loud.

items.title: Sneakers
items.why: Low-top leather or canvas sneakers.
items.tip: One light and one dark pair cover most outfits.

items.title: Boots
items.why: Chelsea or lace-up boots.
items.tip: Treat leather before the rainy season.

items.title: Loafers
items.why: Easy slip-ons that smarten up trousers.
items.tip: Chunky soles suit relaxed trousers.

items.title: Crossbody bags & totes
items.why: Hands-free bags in leather or canvas.
items.tip: Wear the strap so the bag sits at the hip.

items.title: Watches & simple jewellery
items.why: A simple watch, a fine chain or small hoops.
items.tip: Choose one metal tone and repeat it.

shape_notes: Keep volume and detail on top; choose straight bottoms.
Darker trousers with lighter tops create balance.

fit_guide.tip: Pair one roomy piece with one neater piece so the outfit keeps shape.
A slight crop at the ankle suits sneakers and loafers; full length suits boots.
Build around a base tee or shirt, then add an overshirt, knit or jacket.
Stick to two or three palette shades per outfit for easy mixing.
Choose breathable cotton and linen for heat; heavier twill and wool for cooler days.
Relaxed shouldn't mean sloppy — check the shoulders still sit near your shoulder line.

hair.title: Curly top with taper
hair.why: Keeping curls taller than wide adds length.
reasons: Suits the hair texture you told us
hair.tip: Apply curl cream to damp hair and avoid brushing curls when dry.

hair.title: Short twists or natural coils
reasons: Suits the hair texture you told us
hair.tip: Moisturise regularly and sleep on a satin pillowcase to reduce frizz.

hair.title: Textured crop
hair.why: Texture on top adds height; keep the sides short.
hair.tip: Ask for scissor-cut texture on top with a low or mid taper; style with a matte clay.

hair.title: Side part
hair.why: An off-centre part adds asymmetry and length.
hair.tip: A natural part grows out more gracefully than a shaved 'hard' part.

hair_alternatives.title: Quiff
hair_alternatives.why: Lift at the front elongates the face.
hair_alternatives.tip: Blow-dry upwards and finish with a light paste.

hair_alternatives.title: Pompadour
hair_alternatives.why: Height at the crown makes the face look longer.
hair_alternatives.tip: Needs daily styling with a pomade and blow-dryer.

hair_alternatives.title: Fade variations
hair_alternatives.why: A mid or high fade slims the sides.
hair_alternatives.tip: Low fades grow out softer; skin fades need a trim every 2–3 weeks.

eyewear.title: Rectangular frames
eyewear.tip: A slightly wider-than-tall lens suits most faces.

eyewear.title: Browline frames
eyewear.why: The defined upper line adds structure.
eyewear.tip: The top rim should follow your eyebrows.

eyewear.title: Square acetate frames
eyewear.tip: Check that your eyes sit near the centre of each lens.

eyewear.title: Round frames
eyewear.why: Soft circles that contrast with angles.
eyewear.tip: Make sure the frame is about as wide as your face at the temples.

accessories.title: Watches
accessories.why: A rectangular dial adds an angular accent.
accessories.tip: Match the metal to your undertone and the strap to your belt.

accessories.title: Fine chains
accessories.why: A slightly longer chain creates a vertical line.
accessories.tip: Keep it close to the collarbone.

accessories.title: Caps & hats
accessories.tip: Choose crown height to suit your face length.

accessories.title: Bracelets
accessories.tip: Wear on the wrist opposite your watch.

grooming.tip: Short cuts and fades look best trimmed every 2–4 weeks; longer styles every 6–8 weeks.
Matte clay or paste for texture, cream for a natural finish, curl cream for curls — use a pea-sized amount.
If you want tidier brows, remove only stray hairs between them and keep the natural shape.
Wear one watch and keep other accessories to one or two pieces in the same metal tone.
Face soft window light, hold the camera at eye level and wear a solid palette shade near your face.

sections.title: Shaving care
sections.intro: Based on the American Academy of Dermatology's shaving tips.

steps.label: Soften first
steps.detail: Shave after a warm shower, or wet your skin and hair first so hairs are softer.

steps.label: Use a shaving cream or gel
steps.detail: If your skin is sensitive, choose one made for sensitive skin and check the label for 'fragrance-free'.

steps.label: Shave with the grain
steps.detail: Shave in the direction your hair grows and rinse the blade after each swipe.

steps.label: Replace blades often
steps.detail: A dull blade drags and irritates; change the blade or disposable razor every 5–7 shaves.

steps.label: Moisturise afterwards
steps.detail: Finish with your moisturiser to calm and protect freshly shaved skin.

sections.title: Beard-area care
sections.intro: Skin under facial hair still needs cleansing and moisture.

steps.label: Cleanse the beard area
steps.detail: Work your gentle cleanser through the beard to the skin underneath, then rinse well.

steps.label: Moisturise the skin underneath
steps.detail: Massage moisturiser into the skin, not just the hair; a beard oil is optional.

steps.label: Trim on clean, dry hair
steps.detail: Trimming dry hair shows the true length and avoids cutting too short.

products.caution: Patch-test if your skin reacts easily.

ingredients.name: Vitamin B5 (panthenol)
ingredients.why: A humectant often used for comfort and hydration.

products.reason: A gentle general-purpose hydration option for oily skin.

products.caution: Introduce one active at a time and stop if irritation occurs.

ingredients.why: A widely used form of vitamin B3 often chosen for the look of oiliness, pores and marks. Start slowly — higher strengths can sting some skin.
